svg.text: D. Three-Domain Secure (3-D Secure, or 3DS): the bank approval flow
3DS is the card networks' identity check. It asks the card's issuing bank to confirm the shopper really is the cardholder. It never changes the amount.
Shopper presses Pay
The page hands the card to the provider's secure form.
Card data never touches Orvanna's own code.
The processor answers with a status
succeeded, failed, or requires_customer_action.
Frictionless pass, the usual case
Phase one of 3DS is silent: the bank inspects the device
and the transaction and usually approves without asking
anything. The shopper sees nothing at all and the
promise resolves on our own page.
A real challenge
Phase two happens only when the bank wants proof.
It draws a passcode form of its own inside a window
the merchant supplies. We never write, style, or see
the contents of that form.
A blank window is not a challenge
Both phases run inside the same frame, so the frame
appearing means "authentication is running", not "a
challenge is up". So the frame is hidden the instant it
appears and revealed only if it is still there 1,400
milliseconds later. Presentation only; it gates nothing.
Two shapes the window can take
In-page popup (what Orvanna runs today)
The profile setting for iframe redirection is on, so the
shopper stays on orvanna.io through the approval.
Full page redirect (the older fallback)
The bank takes the whole page away with a history
replace, so pressing Back cannot bring it home.
The resume path
The order number rides in the return address, and a copy
is written to storage BEFORE the payment is confirmed,
because a callback may never run. On the way back, the
page shows a complete destination that names the order
and asks our own server what happened. It never says "press Back".
What Orvanna puts around the window
The bank's content cannot be branded or reached into,
so everything around it is ours:
- a bar carrying the test-mode notice, the order number,
and a "Cancel and go back" control
- the checkout behind it genuinely disabled, so no
keyboard user can change the amount being approved
- a focus trap, a dialog role, and a polite live region
- the bar sits at the maximum z-index AND last in the page
The five challenge window sizes
A merchant supplies the WINDOW, not the form.
EMV 3-D Secure 2 permits exactly five sizes:
05 full screen
The bank formats its content to the size asked for.
Why we do not draw the innermost frame
The provider's own widget creates it, because the
widget is what confirms the payment and therefore
what first sees the "needs approval" status.
Taking that away would mean confirming server side,
which would mean the card entering our own page,
which would put this site inside Payment Card
Industry (PCI) scope. Not worth it for a demo.
Four endings, four different sentences
The check could not run
Nothing is wrong with the card. Try again shortly.
The bank did not confirm it was you
Retry the approval, or use a different card.
Confirmed, then the card was declined
Usually a limit or a hold. Telling this shopper to
check their card details is actively wrong.
A plain decline, no approval involved
Try again with a different card.
Every one of them ends "nothing was charged".
Two waiting clocks, because a processor takes seconds and a person reading a text message from their bank takes one to three minutes:
processor wait, every 2 seconds up to 20 seconds. Authentication wait, every 5 seconds for the first minute then every 10, up to 10 minutes.
Sources: www/shop.html (challenge chrome, reveal rule, poll schedule), docs/3DS-RESEARCH.md, ROADMAP.md, functions/create-payment/index.ts
